the development of a new formulation based on the pectin matrix and the use of the synthetic polymer as an additive.
the possibility of applying the pectin beads as a colon targeting drug carrier for 5 ASA.
the possibility of using pectin as a drug carrier for the colon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the release of the 5 ASA from the pectin beads is affected mainly by the presence of the synthetic polymers.
the polymeric coating is a very important factor influencing the release of 6 aminosalicylate.
the polymeric coating of pectin beads with the synthetic polymers is effective in controlling the 5 ASA release.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the release of mesalazine from the beads was controlled by the coating and the presence of the synthetic polymer.
the pectin beads with polymeric coating could be a potential carrier for the drug release to the colon.
the pectin based beads are a suitable drug carrier system and can be used for the controlled release of 5 amino salicylic acid to the colon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
amidated pectin is a suitable polymer for the preparation of beads for colon delivery of 5 ASA.
the release pattern can be controlled by changing the coating composition.
the pectin beads with PA and 5 ASA can be a good alternative to currently available mesalazine formulations.
